description: Realistic benchmark dataset with semantic distractors to stress-test retrieval quality

ingestion_history.content: I am building a Java application with Spring Boot for the backend.
We migrated our production database from MySQL to PostgreSQL last month.
For the frontend we are using React with TypeScript and Vite as the build tool.
My previous project was a Python Flask API with a MongoDB backend.
We deployed the application on AWS using ECS Fargate containers.
The authentication system uses JWT tokens with a 24 hour expiration.
I configured Redis as a caching layer to speed up frequent queries.
Our team follows a two week sprint cycle with standups every morning.
The CI pipeline runs on GitHub Actions with automated test execution.
I enjoy hiking in the mountains on weekends when the weather is nice.
We use pgvector extension in PostgreSQL for storing and searching vector embeddings.
The embedding model we use is text-embedding-ada-002 from OpenAI with 1536 dimensions.
My colleague Sarah handles the DevOps pipeline and infrastructure provisioning.
We started using Kubernetes last quarter but switched back to ECS for simplicity.
The API rate limit is set to 100 requests per minute per user.
I read a Python tutorial about Django REST framework last night for fun.
Database backups run every 6 hours and are stored in S3 with lifecycle policies.
We integrated Sentry for error tracking and Datadog for application monitoring.
The search functionality uses cosine similarity with a threshold of 0.75.
My favorite programming language is Rust but I mostly write Java at work.
We had a database outage last Tuesday that lasted about 45 minutes.
Spring Boot version 3.2 introduced support for virtual threads which we enabled.
The payment integration uses Stripe API for processing credit card transactions.
Our MongoDB instance in the old project was hosted on Atlas with a shared cluster.
Logging is handled by SLF4J with Logback and logs are shipped to CloudWatch.
